key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex problems when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable when momentum is adaptive and coupled with vanishing steps.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning and LLM training, the paper suggests a practical alternative to standard momentum that preserves geometry-aware updates while improving convergence guarantees.
method: Proves fixed-momentum Muon can miss the global optimum on convex Lipschitz objectives for almost all initializations.
Shows asymptotic convergence is recovered when momentum adapts toward 1 with a vanishing step size.
Introduces MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient updates using relative-progress weighting and achieves optimal dimension dependence in convex settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining, supporting MAGD as a simple practical alternative to Muon.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on boundedness and regularity assumptions, so behavior may degrade if iterates or gradients are highly unstable in practice.
